entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The weight metaphor is exact - the other person is pressed down, not persuaded.
examples: insufferably overbearing behavior toward the waiter

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest form: the questions are being asked, and nothing is implied about why.

entries.definition: resembling a beast; showing lack of human sensibility
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and largely trivial now (*beastly weather*); the cruelty has drained out of it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *heedless*: warnings existed and were ignored; it presumes there was something to heed.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names one of the seven deadly sins; the laziness is a fault of the soul.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *cheery*: outward-facing: a cheery greeting is aimed at somebody.

entries.definition: lacking in courage and manly strength and resolution; contemptibly fearful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Bookish contempt - small-spirited in the face of difficulty.

entries.definition: conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Has largely left sound behind; *blatant* now means flagrant, and the loudness is figurative.

entries.definition: having an irritable and unpleasant disposition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Places the fault in the nature, which leaves no room for a bad day.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *earnest*: sincerity that shows its effort, which is why it can be faintly comic.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *clever*: praises ingenuity - though 'too clever' turns it into a fault.

entries.definition: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The refusal is a refusal to be reformed, and the speaker has given up on it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Openly sexist: it casts a wife as the tormentor and a husband as her victim.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise with a shadow: the same word can mean unspoiled or unprepared.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *vulgar*: coarseness with class in it - the offence is against taste as much as manners.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *cunning*: half-admiring when said of animals and plans, condemning when said of people.
examples: had ever circumstances conspired so cunningly?

entries.definition: (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The central moral charge: the suffering was known about and inflicted anyway.

entries.definition: in a disobedient or naughty way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *naughty*: affectionate scolding - too light to carry a real fault.
examples: behaved naughtily when they had guests and was sent to his room

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Wisdom claimed without limit, which is why it turns sarcastic so easily.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm but faintly patronising - the warmth is being observed, not felt.
examples: a round red twinkly Santa Claus

entries.definition: having an abundant supply of money or possessions of value
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Temporarily well supplied - this week, not for life.

entries.definition: believing the worst of human nature and motives; having a sneering disbelief in e.g. selflessness of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The furthest word here: not distrust of a person but of the species.

entries.definition: sufficiently fat so as to have a pleasing fullness of figure
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Kindly - fullness presented as pleasing rather than excessive.
examples: a plump, cheerful woman behind the counter

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *dreadful*: emphatic disapproval with a formal, slightly literary edge.
examples: there was a dreadfully bloody accident on the road this morning

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same refusal to yield, entirely admired - dogged is what stubborn is called when it wins.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The bureaucratic word - a certificate exists somewhere, and the object is the better for it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Said of things rather than people - a false name, a false wall; the object was built to deceive.
examples: a suitcase with a false bottom

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, honest verb. Direct without being cruel; every other word in this family exists because people flinch from it.
examples: He died at home, surrounded by his family.

entries.definition: being of delicate or slender build
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Admiring - thinness with grace built into the word.
examples: she was slender as a willow shoot is slender

entries.definition: not of the highest quality or sophistication
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: From minor-league baseball, and the condescension is built in.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: British slang for sexually attractive - casual and now somewhat dated.

entries.definition: wanting to eat or drink more than one can reasonably consume
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The everyday charge, and one of the first moral words a child is taught.
examples: don't be greedy with the cookies

entries.definition: with modesty; in a modest manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *modest*: the virtue the family is named for: an accurate view of oneself, held without fuss.
examples: the dissertation was entitled, modestly, ‘Remarks about a play by Shakespeare’

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Coarse and common; it dismisses the complaint by the word used to name it.

entries.definition: pleasing by delicacy or grace; not imposing
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Pleasing but slight - delicate rather than striking, and faintly diminishing.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *amiable*: mild, slightly old-fashioned praise; pleasantness rather than depth.
examples: ‘Come and visit me,’ he said amiably

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainer, rarer form of *pitiless*, and a shade cooler.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and everyday; *a bit dodgy* covers everything from a stranger to a knee.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the judgement rather than the intelligence - a wise person can act foolishly.
examples: a foolish risk to take with someone else's money

entries.definition: (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: *Ride roughshod over* - disregard rather than violence.
examples: Stalin's roughshod treatment of the kulaks

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Thin but strong - praises unexpected toughness.
examples: a wiry climber who could hang on all day

entries.definition: marked by refinement in taste and manners
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sets a bar and implies others fall below it; the compliment has a history.

entries.definition: emit a loud, unpleasant kind of laughing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harsh and unpleasant - a laugh that sounds like it enjoys something.
examples: She cackled at her own cruelty.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A vivid old word: the hand is not closed, and neither is the person.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The technical form, at home in theology and in narration.

entries.definition: with diligence; in a diligent manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *diligent*: patience aimed at work, and it praises the steadiness rather than the result.
examples: we may diligently observe the Lord's supper on the first day of the week, diligently preach the gospel, or minister to the saint

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *vociferous*: loud to the point of offence - the outcry is itself the objection.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Luxury with a raised eyebrow: elegance that announces its own price.

entries.definition: being full of or promoting cheer; having or showing good spirits
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The steady everyday word - a disposition rather than a burst of feeling.

entries.definition: quietly and steadily persevering especially in detail or exactness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Patience aimed at work, and it praises the steadiness rather than the result.
